test.q: What does Anki’s iPhone app cost?
test.a: It costs $24.99 once, while Anki on computers and Android is free.

test.q: What does Lucida give up compared with Anki?
test.a: No offline mode, no add-ons, no custom card templates, and no .apkg import.

test.q: Which Lucida features are free?
test.a: Learn mode, live games and sharing are free. Lucida Pro costs $5.99 a month.

test.q: Which apps keep your Anki review history when you switch?
test.a: RemNote and Mochi. The other apps take text, so pictures, sounds and review history usually start over.

test.q: Which AI apps does Lucida show step-by-step setup for?
test.a: Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Gemini and Grok can add the same link, but Lucida has no steps for them.

test.q: What do you do if your private link leaks?
test.a: Open Connect AI and choose Make a new link. The old link stops working right away.

test.q: Which Connect AI settings are off by default?
test.a: “Let me check AI cards first” and “Delete cards.” The rest are on.

test.q: How many cards can your AI add in one request?
test.a: Up to 500. On the free plan, there is no cap on the number of cards.

test.q: What is the difference between Hide one and Hide all?
test.a: With Hide one, only the asked box is covered. With Hide all, every box is covered and one is asked.

test.q: How many boxes can one picture have?
test.a: Up to 30. Each box is its own flashcard with its own schedule.

test.q: Is image occlusion free in Lucida?
test.a: Yes. The free plan includes up to 100 pictures and sounds on cards, and Pro lifts that limit.

test.q: What shapes can Lucida’s image occlusion boxes be?
test.a: Rectangles only. There are no ellipses or free-form shapes, and you can’t group several boxes into one card.

test.q: Can Lucida open Anki’s .apkg files?
test.a: No. Use Anki’s Notes in Plain Text export instead, but review history, pictures and sounds don’t come across.

test.q: What are the steps to move a Quizlet set into Lucida?
test.a: Open a set you made on quizlet.com, choose Export, then Copy text, and paste it into Import cards.

test.q: How many cards can the Import screen take at a time?
test.a: Up to 5,000, so import a bigger file in parts. The first-time setup screen has no such cap.

test.q: What does Export all cards give you in Lucida?
test.a: One file, lucida.json, with every deck, card and review, so your review history goes with you.

test.q: Is Learn mode free?
test.a: Yes. It’s part of Lucida’s free plan, and it needs no paid service to run.

test.q: How many right answers in a row count a card as learned?
test.a: Two. Miss one and the card comes back a few questions later, and its streak starts again.

test.q: Which question type is off until you switch it on?
test.a: Type the answer. It’s used for answers up to 40 characters, and it forgives accents and small typos.

test.q: Does an unfinished Learn session follow you to another device?
test.a: No. It’s saved on the device you’re using, in its browser, so you can pick it up later.

test.q: Is Live free, and how many players can a room hold?
test.a: Yes, it’s free. A room holds up to 60 players.

test.q: What do players need to join a live game?
test.a: A 6-digit code and a name. They need no account.

test.q: How many points is a right answer worth in Live?
test.a: 500 points, plus up to 500 more for answering fast. A wrong answer, or no answer, is worth nothing.

test.q: Does Live grade players or save a report for teachers?
test.a: No. Live isn’t graded and doesn’t save a report for teachers.

test.q: Is a Link only deck shown in Discover or on your profile?
test.a: No. Anyone with the link can open it, but its page asks search engines not to list it.

test.q: Can other people change a deck you share?
test.a: No. They can suggest changes, and you take or skip each one, but only helpers you name can edit it directly.

test.q: What happens to a card you study when the owner changes its answer?
test.a: The card comes back as new, so you learn the right thing. A small fix keeps your schedule for that card.

test.q: What can a deck’s owner see about the people who study it?
test.a: Not their schedule, streak or scores. On Pro, the owner sees only which cards people miss most, as percentages without names.

figs.label: A curve that falls over time, jumps back up at each review, and falls more slowly each time
figs.caption: An illustration of the idea, with no real numbers: each review puts the chance of remembering back at the top, and it falls more slowly each time. The card comes back near your goal (90% by default).

test.q: What does FSRS do after each answer?
test.a: It works out the day you’d still have about a 90% chance of remembering that card, and brings it back then.

test.q: How many new cards a day does Lucida start you at?
test.a: 20 a day. There’s no daily review limit, so everything due is in today’s list.

test.q: How many graded reviews does Pro need to tune FSRS to you?
test.a: 400 graded reviews, at least 100 of them reviews of cards you’d already learned.

test.q: Does Lucida use FSRS-6, the newest version?
test.a: Not yet. Lucida uses FSRS version 5, which has 19 parameters, and the newest version has 21.

test.q: What goes around a word to hide it in a Blank card?
test.a: Double brackets. Each blank can be its own card.

test.q: How many pictures and sounds does Free include?
test.a: Up to 100. A sound card that uses the device’s voice stores no file, so it doesn’t count.

test.q: Is there a language picker on a sound card you make by hand?
test.a: No. The card editor has no language picker, so the device reads the words in its default voice and language.

test.q: What does Lucida not include for language learners?
test.a: Lessons, grammar notes, a dictionary, ready-made word lists and native-speaker recordings. It doesn’t grade your pronunciation.

test.q: Which plan lets you set a test date, and what does it do?
test.a: Pro. From 30 days out, the cards you’d likely forget by test day come up early.

test.q: What do flashcards cover for the MCAT?
test.a: Recall, not the whole exam. Use cards for recall and practice for application.

test.q: Is the research on flashcards and exam scores about the MCAT?
test.a: No. The studies we read on flashcards and exam scores are about medical-school exams, not the MCAT.

test.q: Does Lucida include MCAT content or practice questions?
test.a: No. It has no MCAT content or practice questions, and it isn’t affiliated with the AAMC.

test.q: What went with about one more Step 1 point in the 2015 survey?
test.a: Each extra 445 board-style practice questions, or 1,700 unique Anki flashcards. The authors called the study exploratory.

test.q: Does the 2026 review show that Anki use causes higher Step 1 scores?
test.a: No. The evidence is largely observational, so it shows a link, not a cause.

test.q: Is image occlusion free, and how many boxes can one picture hold?
test.a: Yes, it’s free. A picture holds up to 30 boxes, and each box is its own card with its own schedule.

test.q: Can Lucida open Anki’s .apkg decks or run Anki add-ons?
test.a: No. It fits best if you make your own cards instead of studying someone else’s mega-deck.

test.q: What does Lucida Pro cost?
test.a: $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year, as of September 2026. The pricing page has no separate student plan.

test.q: How many pictures and sounds does the Free plan include?
test.a: Up to 100. Pro has no 100 limit.

test.q: What should you use, besides flashcards, for anything you have to work out?
test.a: Past papers or problem sets. Flashcards are for recall.

test.q: Which students remembered more in Roediger and Karpicke’s 2006 experiments?
test.a: Students who tested themselves remembered much more after two days and a week than students who restudied.

test.q: Is Lucida free for teachers?
test.a: Yes. Shared decks and live games are free, and the pricing page has no separate school plan.

test.q: What do students need to join a live game?
test.a: A 6-digit code and a name. They need no account.

test.q: What can a teacher see about how students are doing?
test.a: Not a student’s schedule, streak or scores. On Pro, a deck you share shows which cards people miss most, as percentages without names.

test.q: What does Lucida not do for teachers?
test.a: No gradebook, roster import, or link to school systems. Live games aren’t graded, and it isn’t for students under 13.

test.q: What does Quizlet’s free plan give you in Learn and Test?
test.a: Learn is for Plus subscribers, with a free study session to try it. Test gives one free practice test per set.

test.q: What does Lucida’s free plan include?
test.a: Unlimited decks and cards, FSRS reviews, Learn mode, live games for up to 60 friends, sharing, and import and export.

test.q: When is Quizlet still the right pick?
test.a: When you need the biggest library of ready-made sets, teacher tools, offline iPhone and Android apps, or Classic Quizlet Live.

test.q: Which Quizlet sets can you export?
test.a: Only sets you made, as text without images. You can’t export a set you copied from someone else.

test.q: Is Anki free?
test.a: Mostly. It is free on Windows, Mac, Linux and Android, but AnkiMobile, the iPhone and iPad app, costs $24.99, paid once.

test.q: Which app works offline, Anki or Lucida?
test.a: Anki does: your collection lives on your device. Lucida needs an internet connection.

test.q: What does Anki need to connect to Claude or ChatGPT?
test.a: An add-on and your own API key. In Lucida, your own AI connects through one link and a sign-in.

test.q: Can Lucida read Anki’s .apkg deck files?
test.a: No. Export Notes in Plain Text from Anki instead, but pictures, sounds, tags and your review history don’t come across.

A public deck in Lucida

test.q: Does Brainscape use FSRS to plan reviews?
test.a: No. You rate every card 1 to 5, and Brainscape’s own algorithm picks when it comes back.

test.q: What are Brainscape’s Certified flashcards?
test.a: Expert-curated decks for hundreds of subjects and high-stakes exams. They need Pro, and Lucida has none.

test.q: Can you add pictures and sounds on Brainscape’s free plan?
test.a: No, images and audio are Pro. Lucida’s free plan allows up to 100 pictures and sounds.

test.q: What are Brainscape Pro’s monthly and yearly prices in its App Store listing?
test.a: $19.99 a month or $95.99 a year. Lucida Pro is $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year.

test.q: How many players can join a Gizmo Live game?
test.a: There is no maximum, and it needs at least 2 players. Lucida Live takes up to 60.

test.q: What daily limits does Gizmo’s free plan have?
test.a: 15 hearts, then a 10-minute wait, 2 Magic Imports a day, 20 minutes apart. Lucida has no hearts; Free allows 3 makes a day.

test.q: Can you export your cards from Gizmo?
test.a: Not yet, says Gizmo’s help center. Lucida exports every deck as CSV and everything, reviews included, as JSON.

test.q: What can Gizmo’s Magic Import turn into cards?
test.a: PDFs, recordings, photos, PowerPoint files, websites and YouTube links. You don’t need a separate AI subscription.

test.a: Yes. Knowt’s Ultra plan removes them, and Lucida shows no ads, free or Pro.

test.q: What does Knowt Ultra cost?
test.a: $149.99 a year with a 3-day free trial, or $24.99 a month.

test.q: How many AI summaries does Knowt’s free plan allow?
test.a: 1 summary a month. On Free, Lucida lets your own AI make as many cards as you want.

test.q: What AI tools does Knowt have built in?

test.q: What does Mochi’s free plan include?
test.a: Unlimited cards and decks, offline use, import and export, and no sign-up.

test.q: What does Mochi Pro cost?
test.a: $5 a month billed yearly ($60), or $6 a month billed monthly. Pro adds sync, publishing decks and more AI.

test.q: Is sync free on Lucida?
test.a: Yes: sign in and your cards are on every device. On Mochi, sync is part of Pro.

test.q: Can Mochi import Anki .apkg files?
test.a: Yes, including review history. Lucida can’t read .apkg files.

test.q: What does Quizlet’s free plan give you for Learn and Test?
test.a: A free study session for Learn, and one free practice test per set for Test. Lucida’s Learn mode is free.

test.q: Which Quizlet features are paid only?
test.a: Diagram sets, rich text, offline studying and an ad-free experience. Lucida has no ads, free or Pro.

test.q: Which app has the bigger library of shared decks, Quizlet or Lucida?
test.a: Quizlet, with millions of public sets. Lucida’s library of shared decks is new and much smaller.

test.q: Does Quizlet have spaced repetition?
test.a: Yes, but on its website only. Lucida plans every review with FSRS, in any browser.

test.q: Where do RemNote cards live?
test.a: Inside your notes. Any bullet can become a card: type Question == Answer.

test.q: What does RemNote Pro cost a month?
test.a: $10 a month, or $8 a month billed yearly. Lucida Pro is $5.99 a month, but the plans include different things.

test.q: How many image-occlusion images does RemNote’s free plan allow?
test.a: 5 images. Lucida’s free plan has up to 100 pictures and sounds.

test.q: Does RemNote work offline?
test.a: Yes, in the desktop and mobile apps, but it is limited in the web app. Lucida has no offline mode.
